subject: Milestone-driven credit allocation & billing cadence for accelerator cohort
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma@prodseed.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alan Cho <alan@prodseed.io>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Accelerator cohort — can we align credits to milestone payouts?

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the chat last week. Quick follow-up from our side — ProdSeed runs cohorts where startups hit discrete milestones (incorporation, first 1k MAU, $10k ARR). We’d like to propose milestone-triggered credit disbursements rather than a single upfront allotment. That helps us both align usage and avoid waste across teams.

High-level ask: would Redwood consider a milestone-driven credit schedule that: 1) releases 40% of the cohort credits at kick-off, 2) 30% when the cohort reaches the first product milestone, and 3) the remaining 30% after demo day? We’d also like invoicing to follow quarterly for administrative simplicity (we issue a single PO per cohort).

We can share a short spreadsheet with dates and cohort sizes if that helps. Also copying Alan — he handles operations and PO processing.

Appreciate any flexibility here — ProdSeed is targeting 25 startups for the next cohort and this could scale with renewal.

Best,
Emma Liu
Director, Partnerships
ProdSeed Labs

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@prodseed.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Alan Cho <alan@prodseed.io>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Accelerator cohort — can we align credits to milestone payouts?

Emma — thanks, this makes sense and happy to explore.

A few quick notes from Redwood on feasibility:
- Milestone-driven allocation is doable from a tooling perspective; we can create credit buckets and tie releases to dates or HubSpot webhook events.
- For billing, we prefer to issue a single invoice per cohort per quarter, but we can support a PO that references a credit schedule.
- We typically require a small administrative fee for split allocations (covers accounting reconciliation). I’ll propose a model below.

Proposal (initial):
1) Credit Pool: Redwood issues a total committed credit pool to ProdSeed for the cohort (example: $15k equivalent per startup x 25 = $375k).
2) Release Schedule: 40% at kickoff, 30% at milestone 1 (proof-of-concept), 30% at demo day. Each release is triggered by an Ops confirmation email to billing@redwood.ai.
3) Billing: Redwood invoices ProdSeed quarterly for the amount of credits released in that quarter. If a release crosses invoice boundaries, we prorate on the next invoice.
4) Administrative Fee: 2% of the committed pool to cover split allocation & extra reporting (waivable for first cohort as a pilot).
5) Overage and conversion: If a startup exhausts credits, usage continues at standard pay-as-you-go rates unless the startup converts to a paid account (we can include conversion credits as a sweetener).

I’ve attached a simple credit schedule spreadsheet and an MSA redline to start the legal conversation. If you can push the cohort dates and expected milestone windows into the spreadsheet, we’ll create a formal SOW and PO-ready invoice template.

If this looks okay I’ll loop in Finance and Legal for a short one-hour call tomorrow afternoon to finalize terms.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198

Looping in a couple of legal/ops considerations here — high-level thoughts for the call:

1) Revenue recognition — Finance will prefer that the committed pool be recognized on delivery of each milestone (so quarterly invoices are fine), but we need explicit acceptance criteria for each milestone to avoid disputes. Recommend a one-line acceptance checkbox on the Ops confirmation email: "Milestone X confirmed by ProdSeed Ops (name + date)".

2) PO language — ask ProdSeed to include the cohort ID and Redwood deal_id (PSL-2026-11-02) on the PO so matching is straightforward.

3) Administrative fee — I can approve waiving the 2% fee for the pilot cohort if we get a renewal commitment (simple term: >50% renew cohort within 12 months).

4) Edge cases — If startups churn before demo day, remaining unreleased credits should be returned to Redwood and reallocated for future cohorts unless ProdSeed requests to convert them to a paid use-case (chargeable).

Ben — if you share a draft SOW and the Ops confirmation template before the call, I’ll bring a one-pager so Legal can approve the PO flow.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of GTM Programs, Redwood Inference
